domains.name: Biodiversity and Conservation in the Philippines

standards.text: traits are passed from parents to offspring through genes, and that variations in DNA result in observable differences among individuals and populations;
natural variation in inherited traits contributes to biodiversity, and that endemic organisms play important roles in maintaining ecosystems and supporting community life; and
biotechnology, supported by digital tools for analyzing biological information, is applied in everyday life to improve human health, food production, and community well-being.
natural resources are essential for daily living and that sustainable practices help reduce environmental impact and ensure resource availability for present and future needs;
human activities release pollutants and greenhouse gases that contribute to climate change, which affects ecosystems and communities at local and global levels;
space technologies, including satellites and space probes, provide important data that help scientists understand Earth’s systems, environmental changes, and the universe;

The learners can design practical and simple solutions or awareness activities that demonstrate understanding of heredity, biodiversity, and biotechnology and their applications in improving everyday life in the community.

The learners can design and communicate simple, evidence-based explanations or proposals that demonstrate understanding of environmental sustainability, climate change, and the role of space technologies in monitoring Earth and improving daily life.

competencies.text: identify patterns of inherited traits in familiar human characteristics (e.g., dimples, widow’s peak, attached or free earlobes, and other inherited traits) using simple family examples or pedigrees to explain that genes are passed from parents to offspring;
explain that differences in physical characteristics among people (e.g., skin tone, height, hair type and other inherited traits) are features of genetic diversity resulting from variations in DNA;
explain that natural variation in inherited traits contributes to the variety of plants and animals found in the Philippines;
describe endemic organisms in the Philippines by identifying examples found in their locality or nearby regions and explaining their importance to local ecosystems and communities;
design a community-based activity that helps protect and preserve local biodiversity and describe how it can be applied in the community;
describe the importance and everyday uses of traditional biotechnology (e.g., fermentation in food production, preservation, and household practices);
describe how biotechnology helps improve crop production and nutritional value to support food needs;

explain how biotechnology, supported by digital tools for analyzing biological information, help scientists develop medicines, vaccines, and medical technologies that address health problems in communities; and
explain how the responsible and ethical use of biotechnology can support community well-being while minimizing risks to health, society, and the environment.

explain how conserving natural resources (e.g., water, energy, raw materials) helps reduce environmental damage, maintain resource availability, and support daily needs such as food production, energy use, and clean water supply;

identify ways to practice environmental sustainability in everyday life and describe how these actions (e.g., waste reduction, energy and water conservation, use of renewable energy, and sustainable food practices) help protect the environment;

explain how human activities such as fossil fuel burning, deforestation, industrial processes, and mining contribute to climate change by releasing greenhouse gases and other pollutants that affect the environment;
describe how greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere and how increased greenhouse gas levels enhance the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming;

use information from reliable data sources (e.g., online databases) to analyze how climate change affects local communities and ecosystems, and relate these effects to global phenomena such as sea-level rise and increased frequency of extreme weather events;
identify Filipino and international contributions to space technologies and describe how these advancements benefit society (e.g., communication, weather forecasting, disaster monitoring);
use information from satellite images, weather maps, and online databases (e.g., PAGASA, NASA, PhilSA) to explain how satellites collect and provide data about
explain how robotic rovers and probes collect data from planets such as Mars and how these findings contribute to understanding Earth’s formation, environment, and processes; and
explain how scientists estimate the scale of the universe using ground-based and space-based technologies (e.g., telescopes and measurements of redshift and standard candles).
